title: HealthFraudML: Open-Source Healthcare Fraud Detection Framework
description:
HealthFraudML is a modular Python framework for healthcare claims fraud detection. It provides a unified API over supervised, unsupervised and hybrid machine-learning models; fraud-type detectors for upcoding, unbundling, duplicate claims and phantom billing; a rule-based patient billing auditor that flags upcoding, unbundling and charges far above a disclosed review threshold, and drafts a dispute letter; and an organizational readiness assessment. Explanations for flagged cases are derived from each model's own feature importances; SHAP and LIME are not used by the package.

The repository ships a price benchmark of 7,359 separately payable CPT/HCPCS codes derived from the public CMS Physician Fee Schedule Relative Value File (PPRRVU25_JAN.csv, conversion factor 32.3465), and 8,387 plain-language code names ingested from the public CMS quarterly alpha-numeric HCPCS file. Both carry code numbers and CMS payment amounts only; no AMA CPT descriptors are distributed. A separate 8-model comparison script evaluates the models on the public Kaggle Healthcare Provider Fraud Detection dataset and on a synthetic generator whose parameters are hand-chosen and illustrative rather than calibrated to real claims data.

Two components are present but not implemented: the identity-theft detector is a stub that always returns no findings, and no kickback detector exists. The anonymization module performs Safe Harbor-style identifier removal and generalization but does not provide a k-anonymity guarantee.
